styleSelection.reason: Requested pen plus light wash: connected roof and wall junctions describe the village; transparent warm stone and grouped olive-green washes preserve the sunlit paths. Use the supplied ink-and-wash value floor at reduced strength so cypresses remain legible.

families.referenceCue: Small distant ochre houses with terracotta roofs: pale warm planes, thin dry pen at roof junctions, reduced detail.
Three stepped houses on the right: light ochre walls, sienna roofs, violet-grey shadow sides; pen defines eaves and wall corners, selective openings last.
Sunlit limestone terrace walls and winding pale paths: broad dilute warm washes, paper gaps and broken edges, no masonry hatching.
Interlocking olive crowns alternate yellow-green sun and cool grey-green shade. Paint connected crown groups and then one connected dry shadow glaze; preserve light gaps, no leaf dots.
Tall narrow blue-green cypresses punctuate the warm terraces; keep tapering silhouettes, reserve adjacent pale stone, shade the dark side after drying.
Foreground open pine has a dark leaning trunk and branching rhythm below a light olive canopy. Thin directional branch ink over connected transparent foliage, never ink filling a crown.
Pale winding path descends between olive trees; keep the connected light corridor and paint the crossing tree shadows as a dry glaze.
Distant blue-grey olive grove in upper right is a pale wash with quiet edges, no individual branches or pen texture.

reserves.reason: Bare paper sliver on sunlit right roof ridge
